newsitem.title: LESOTHO: S.Africa pledges to support Lesotho in police siege.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa pledges to support Lesotho in police siege.

text.p: South Africa's foreign minister said on Sunday his country would support the Lesotho government in defusing the siege of the police headquarters taken over by eight members of the Royal Lesotho Mounted Police.

Despite negotiations with the government and church leaders, the eight officers -- who are resisting arrest over the killing of three fellow officers in October 1995 -- still controlled the command in the capital Maseru for the fourth day on Sunday.

"The matter is receiving urgent attention. We're fully in support of the democratically elected government in Lesotho," Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo said in Namibia, where he is at a Southern Africa Development Community (SADC) conference.

He did not explain what kind of support was meant, but foreign ministry spokesman Pieter Swanepoel disputed a newspaper report that South African police specialising in hostage situations and urban warfare had been placed on standby.
Swanepoel said the South African government did not yet see the situation as a crisis because the Lesotho government was not affected by the siege.
Nzo was constantly being updated on any new developments by Lesotho ministers also at the conference, Swanepoel added.
A Lesotho government statement on Saturday said the mutineers had "attempted to relieve a number of senior officers of their duties" since taking over the station on Thursday.
State radio quoted the dissidents as saying they had rounded up the senior officers, including the acting police commissioner, and dismissed them.
They said they would also sack the police commissioner of the tiny landlocked mountain kingdom when he returned from Namibia.
The mutineering officers are claiming amnesty under Lesotho's Pardons Act, which stipulates that security force members may not be charged for any crimes committed from 1993 to 1995.
"This illegal action appears to have been taken as an attempt to further delay the appearance of the suspected officers in court," the statement said.

Local news reports said the officers were also retaliating for the alleged killing of a junior policeman who had supported their refusal to stand trial. He was gunned down at his Maseru home last weekend.
